title: Factors for Lower Hiring Rate of Persons with Disabilities in Public Sector Compared to Private Sector
what_it_is: Factors for Lower Hiring Rate of Persons with Disabilities in Public Sector Compared to Private Sector

sections.label: PwD employment rate focus
sections.summary: The Government focuses on raising PwD employment rates, but public sector roles requiring fitness and lack of comparative data may cause differing hiring rates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Government is focused on raising the overall employment rate of PwDs across both the public and private sectors, where PwDs are placed and retained in jobs that are best suited to their strengths and capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: However, the public sector also has a significant proportion of roles for which a certain level of physical and mental fitness is required, such as the uniformed services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: This is one reason why hiring rates of PwDs may differ across sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: There is also no comparative data for the hiring rates of PwDs in the public sector across developed countries.

sections.label: Meaningful jobs for PwDs
sections.summary: The Public Service commits to making every job count for employed PwDs, based on capabilities, and says public and private sector jobs are not comparable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For us, it is more important to make sure that instead of counting the number of jobs, it is to make every job count.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And that is what the Public Service sector is prepared and is committed to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We want to make sure that every PwD employed by the Public Service sector has a meaningful job, based on their capabilities and strengths, and we will continue to look out for jobs where we can meaningfully employ PwDs to best make use of their talents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And I think all my agencies are trying their best to make sure that they can convert jobs that are relevant and meaningful for us to hire PwDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I have said that there are many jobs in the Public Service sector that are not comparable with the jobs in the private sector, and it is not meaningful for us to make that comparison.

sections.label: Agencies and transport sector
sections.summary: The passage names the National Library Board, VITAL, GovTech, CPF Board, MSF, MOH Holdings, Singapore General Hospital and the transport sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Just to name a few: the National Library Board, VITAL, GovTech, the Central Provident Fund Board, Ministry of Social and Family Development, Ministry of Health Holdings, Singapore General Hospital and also the transport sector.

sections.label: No artificial targets or tokenism
sections.summary: Because job nature differs, the passage says artificial targets or tokenism should not be used just to meet targets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But as I have mentioned, the nature of the jobs is quite different.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, we should not set artificial targets or we should not do what we call "tokenism", just to meet targets.
